subject: 20260913-175934-sweep-deepgram-30
headline: The voice agent maintains steady conversational latency up to concurrency 20 with 100.0% setup success, but experiences a significant tail latency spike on the final closing turn.

insights.title: Tail Latency Spike on Closing Turn
insights.finding: The final turn of the conversation, where the caller finishes the interaction, experiences a severe tail latency spike of 3182.2 ms at the 95th percentile, while earlier turns remain near 1017.6 ms.
insights.why_it_matters: A delay over 3000 ms at the end of a call creates an awkward silence and makes the agent feel unresponsive right before the hang-up.
insights.next_step: Investigate potential backend system cleanups, final state saves, or database commits triggered specifically on the final confirmation turn to eliminate this lag.

insights.title: Invalid Concurrency 40 Test Due to Degraded Harness
insights.finding: The test machine degraded during the concurrency 40 step, meaning we can draw no performance conclusions about the agent at this scale because the measurements reflect runner limits rather than agent capacity.
insights.why_it_matters: Without a healthy test runner at this concurrency level, we cannot verify the true breaking point or high-load performance of the agent.
insights.next_step: Rerun the load test at concurrency 40 using a healthy, non-degraded test runner.

insights.title: Steady Core Latency Up to Concurrency 20
insights.finding: Median wait time before speaking remains highly stable and healthy under rising load, moving from 841.5 ms at baseline down to 792.9 ms at concurrency 20.
insights.why_it_matters: The agent's core routing and speech engine handles moderate load without showing signs of scaling bottlenecks or queueing.
insights.next_step: Keep monitoring latency trends to ensure this stability continues as user concurrency scales further.

insights.title: Word Error Rate Rises Slightly Under Load
insights.finding: The average word error rate (wer), representing words misheard by the agent, increases from 2.6% at baseline to 3.8% at concurrency 20.
insights.why_it_matters: While still very low, this upward trend suggests that increased concurrency might be introducing subtle speech-to-text processing or audio packet handling issues under load.
insights.next_step: Investigate audio streaming quality and packet loss behavior at concurrency levels above 20.

insights.title: Inconclusive Latency and Quality Correlation
insights.finding: The automated judge evaluated only 20 calls out of 210 total calls and could not draw a conclusive correlation between high latency and task failures.
insights.why_it_matters: With only 20 calls evaluated, we do not have a large enough sample size to trust that slower agent responses are not negatively impacting task success.
insights.next_step: Configure the automated judge to grade a larger percentage of calls from the higher concurrency steps.
